hazard_consequence_node.label: HazardConsequence
hazard_consequence_node.name: Dust explosion
hazard_consequence_node.evidence: The Executive Summary states: "A February 20, 2003, dust explosion at the CTA Acoustics, Inc. facility in Corbin, Kentucky, killed seven and injured 37 workers." It also states that "combustible phenolic resin dust that had accumulated throughout the facility fueled the explosion." The incident description further says that the initial explosion and later secondary explosions were caused when dispersed combustible dust ignited.
hazard_consequence_node.explanation: The report’s main analysis centers on combustible phenolic resin dust accumulation, dispersion during cleaning, ignition near line 405, and propagation into secondary dust explosions across the facility. This makes dust explosion the primary hazard consequence, while fires, fireballs, and confined effects are escalation phenomena within the same dust-explosion event sequence.

entity_nodes.label: Material
entity_nodes.name: Phenolic resin dust
entity_nodes.evidence: a combustible phenolic resin dust fueled the fire and explosions.
entity_nodes.explanation: Phenolic resin dust was the combustible material that accumulated, dispersed, and ignited, driving the dust explosion sequence.

entity_nodes.label: Location
entity_nodes.name: line 405 oven
entity_nodes.evidence: the initial explosion’s point of origin was likely in the aisle on the east side of the line 405 oven, near the south end.
entity_nodes.explanation: The fire and initial explosion originated at the line 405 oven area.

entity_nodes.label: Location
entity_nodes.name: line 405 baghouse
entity_nodes.evidence: the transition leading to the baghouse was plugged.
entity_nodes.explanation: The line 405 baghouse and its transition were involved in the dust-release conditions during cleaning.

condition_nodes.label: Phase
condition_nodes.name: Solid
condition_nodes.explanation: The hazardous material was present as solid particulate dust.

condition_nodes.label: Temperature
condition_nodes.name: High temperature
condition_nodes.evidence: the oven was running too hot.
condition_nodes.explanation: The dust cloud formed near an operating curing oven that was reported to be running too hot.

condition_nodes.label: Combustibility
condition_nodes.name: Combustible
condition_nodes.evidence: combustible phenolic resin dust that had accumulated throughout the facility fueled the explosion.
condition_nodes.explanation: The phenolic resin dust was capable of burning and exploding when dispersed and ignited.

condition_nodes.label: ReleaseType
condition_nodes.name: Continuous release
condition_nodes.evidence: the poor functioning of the baghouse and resulting lack of suction in the mat-former caused excessive release of dust from the production line.
condition_nodes.explanation: Dust was released over the course of cleaning and poor dust-collection performance rather than by a single vessel rupture.

condition_nodes.label: Confinement
condition_nodes.name: High confinement
condition_nodes.evidence: Explosion overpressure originated in area between oven and wall and in partially enclosed area above blend room and below ceiling
condition_nodes.explanation: The dust ignited inside the building in partially enclosed areas that increased explosion overpressure.

condition_nodes.label: Dispersion
condition_nodes.name: Dispersed
condition_nodes.evidence: generated a cloud of combustible dust around line 405.
condition_nodes.explanation: Cleaning and blowdown activities suspended settled dust into the air before ignition.

event_nodes.label: InitiatingEvent
event_nodes.name: Compressed-air cleaning dispersed combustible dust into the production area
event_nodes.evidence: Those operators used a compressed air lance to blow the remaining material out of the transition. That material fell back through a chute into the production area.
event_nodes.explanation: During routine cleaning with the oven operating, compressed-air blowdown and related cleaning activities dispersed combustible dust and initiated the accident sequence.

event_nodes.label: MechanicalFailure
event_nodes.name: Poor functioning of line 405 baghouse
event_nodes.evidence: the poor functioning of the baghouse and resulting lack of suction in the mat-former caused excessive release of dust from the production line.
event_nodes.explanation: The baghouse malfunction reduced dust collection effectiveness and contributed directly to excessive dust release around line 405.

event_nodes.label: IgnitionSource
event_nodes.name: Unknown ignition source
event_nodes.evidence: Flames may have escaped through an open oven door, or the dust cloud may have entered the oven and ignited.
event_nodes.explanation: Ignition clearly occurred near the operating line 405 oven, but the exact ignition source could not be determined from the investigation.
